comment: THE UNREACHED-LEG REGISTER. A leg is one site in a guard script that can drive a non-zero exit and says so with its own message; its identity is the longest static run in that message -- the substring a test can assert. Legs are PARSED FROM SOURCE by tests/compliance/_legs.ts -- which is itself in this register, because an instrument exempt from its own standard is what the register exists to stop -- never declared, because a hand-maintained ledger drifts from the code it describes and that is the defect this register exists to prevent, one level in. A leg is REACHED only when some test, in ANY directory under tests/ that holds test files, asserts a substring of its own message through an EXECUTED assertion -- toContain, or toThrow where the failure is raised rather than printed -- not when it merely makes the guard exit non-zero, and not when the message appears in a test header comment. Recognising only one spelling of an assertion is a defect this parser has already had to fix four times, so the set is widened when a legitimate assertion is written a new way, never narrowed to force a style. tests/compliance/leg_coverage.test.ts holds the ratchet: a new leg with no entry reds, an entry for a leg that no longer exists reds, and a registered leg that HAS become reached reds so the entry is forced out. EVIDENCE SCOPE IS DISCOVERED, NOT LISTED: evidenceDirs() in tests/compliance/_legs.ts returns every directory under tests/ holding at least one *.test.ts, so a plant in tests/db or tests/e2e counts and a directory added tomorrow counts without anyone updating a list. It read tests/compliance ALONE until 2026-09-12, which meant a guard exercisable only against a live database could never be recorded as proved however thoroughly it was planted. SCRIPT SCOPE, stated because a description broader than its filter is section 2(d) of .claude/rules/test-conventions.md: this covers GUARD SCRIPTS in scripts/ (.sh and .mjs) plus the two instrument files named in tests/compliance/leg_coverage.test.ts. Application code -- packages/auth, packages/gate, packages/snapshot -- is NOT in this corpus and is not claimed to be; it is covered by its own tests, not by a leg ratchet.

baseline_2026_09_10.note: A separate hand audit counted 79 legs and 5 reached, using a looser rule: per-pattern granularity for data-driven loops, and crediting a plant that asserts its own planted DATA (a filename, a planted column name) rather than the leg message. Both numbers are real. This register enforces the strict rule, which is why its starting figure is lower.
baseline_2026_09_10.immutable: THIS IS A HISTORICAL RECORD AND DOES NOT MOVE. The ratchet asserts the CURRENT reached count is >= this figure, so progress is free and regression is not. Restating it would destroy the only number that says where this started.

current.note: 2026-09-23, R-2026-09-23-65 A2: scripts/lint_public_table_rls.sh now LEXES each migration (an embedded perl lexer) and classifies every form that can create or move a table into public -- UNLOGGED, quoted identifiers, SET SCHEMA public, CREATE TABLE ... AS, SELECT INTO, a statement split across lines, foreign tables, IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, extensions, dynamic SQL -- pairing each or refusing it by name. Its four line-grep could-not-run legs went with the line-grep, all registered. Ten legs are new: nine reached by plants in tests/compliance/lint_public_table_rls.test.ts, including the lexer that did not run, reached through a stub perl on PATH rather than registered; one registered, a pattern that cannot compile. legs_total 233 -> 239, reached 204 -> 213, registered 29 -> 26. PREVIOUS NOTE: 2026-09-22, R-2026-09-22-56 C: scripts/lint_public_table_rls.sh joins the register and the aggregator -- every table created in schema public must ENABLE and FORCE row level security in the SAME file. Six legs reached, four registered could-not-run (the scan-exited branches, the same seam lint_no_replica_identity_full.sh's equivalent waits on). legs_total 223 -> 233, reached 198 -> 204, registered 25 -> 29. PREVIOUS NOTE: 2026-09-22, R-2026-09-22-57 B: the deploy wrapper takes an APP argument and reads its Pages project and build output directory from apps/<app>/wrangler.toml, adding six refusals -- an unrecognised app, a wrangler.toml naming no project, one naming no output directory, no app named at all, an unknown option, and a third positional. All six are reached: each has a plant in tests/compliance/deploy_guards.test.ts that also asserts wrangler was never reached, so a refusal cannot pass by happening after the upload. Note the unknown-option leg's identity carries $1 and so can never equal its own run-time text; its test asserts both forms. The wrapper also gained the STAMP READBACK: four more refusals covering a build that wrote no stamp, a stamp naming another commit (the stale build directory), a stamp marked dirty, and a stamp that could not be read at all -- the last exits 2, because a readback that did not run is a different outcome from one that ran and refused. legs_total 213 -> 223, reached 188 -> 198, registered unchanged at 25. current.registered itself became an asserted figure in this change; it had been a number in the register that no test derived. PREVIOUS NOTE: THE 2026-09-20 MOVE 201 -> 213 / 179 -> 188 IS TWELVE NEW LEGS FROM THE DEPLOY PATH (R-2026-09-20-30): scripts/deploy_pages.sh, which refuses a dirty tree, a HEAD that is not an ancestor of origin/main, an unfetchable origin, an empty --branch and a non-repository; scripts/stamp_build.mjs, which refuses rather than stamping a build it cannot identify; and run_e2e.sh's refusal of a missing golden path, added when that runner stopped naming two files and started discovering its corpus. Nine are proved by plants in tests/compliance/deploy_guards.test.ts and tests/compliance/build_stamp.test.ts; three are registered, all of the could-not-run family -- they fire only when ONE git subcommand fails after earlier ones succeeded, and no seam here breaks a single subcommand. PREVIOUS NOTE: THE 2026-09-19 MOVE 198 -> 201 / 176 -> 179 IS THREE NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE (R-2026-09-18-17): scripts/lint_no_secrets.sh gained a LOCATION half -- no credential file may be tracked, whatever it holds -- with three failure sites: a tracked credential file, a git ls-files that could not run (not a repository, or a corrupt index), and a repository with nothing tracked. Each is planted in tests/compliance/no_secrets.test.ts. No existing leg changed state. PREVIOUS NOTE: THE 2026-09-18 MOVE 194 -> 198 / 172 -> 176 IS FOUR NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE (A1 sprint, Bundle 1): the service-role bundle guard gained a server-side corpus -- the built Pages Functions output -- and with it three shell legs (an unbuilt functions/ directory, the server-side FAILED verdict, and a server-side scan that could not run) and one scanner leg (a committed literal in server-side code), each planted in tests/compliance/bundle_guards.test.ts. The scanner's usage message changed and its entry was renamed, not added. The client-bundle FAIL leg, which a ternary had hidden from the leg parser, is back as its own failure site. PREVIOUS NOTE: THE 2026-09-18 MOVE 191 -> 194 / 169 -> 172 IS THREE NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE (R-2026-09-18-15): tests/compliance/_legs.ts now reads test files AND instrument files with TypeScript's own parser instead of regex over raw text, and its three refusals -- a test file that will not parse, a parser exposing no parseDiagnostics, and an instrument file that will not parse -- are planted in tests/compliance/leg_coverage.test.ts. The 191 pre-existing legs are unchanged: both rewritten functions were run over main's tree before anything else changed and reproduced main's register output, leg for leg. PREVIOUS NOTE: THE 2026-09-16 MOVE 183 -> 191 / 161 -> 169 IS EIGHT NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE: scripts/freeze_applied_migrations.mjs is the recorder for the frozen boundary (ruling R-2026-09-16-03), run by hand once per hosted apply from runbook step 5, so nothing else exercises its refusals. tests/compliance/freeze_applied_migrations.test.ts plants every one -- no arguments, a malformed date, a non-integer ledger count, a count disagreeing with the repository, and an empty migration directory -- and asserts each message. The script takes an optional repository root as its FOURTH argument for the same reason every lint in scripts/ takes one as $1: without that seam the empty-directory refusal could not be reached by a plant, because a plant is by construction not this repository. The registered count does not move and no leg elsewhere changed state. MEASURED, and updated whenever legs are added or closed. THE 2026-09-14 MOVE 126 -> 136 / 105 -> 115 IS TEN NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE: scripts/attest_counts.mjs gained five refusals -- no closing </testsuites>, no declared root totals, and declared tests / failures / errors disagreeing with the file -- each with two failure messages, and tests/compliance/attest_counts.test.ts plants every one and asserts both lines. The registered count does not move, no leg elsewhere changed state, and the ruler did not change. THE 2026-09-13 MOVE 115 -> 126 / 94 -> 105 IS ELEVEN NEW LEGS, ALL PROVED IN THE SAME CHANGE: scripts/get_extra_search_path.sh arrived with a plant asserting every one of its failure messages, so the registered count does not move. No leg elsewhere changed state and the ruler did not change. The baseline above is the historical record and does not move; the ratchet asserts current.reached >= baseline.reached, so progress is free and regression is not. Restating the baseline would destroy the only number that says where this started. THE 2026-09-12 MOVE 82 -> 86 IS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE: three legs on run_migrations.sh were newly PROVED by plants written in that change, and one -- "no forward migrations found in" -- flipped SOLELY because the evidence corpus widened to reach tests/db. That fourth leg had been proved by tests/db/migration_runner_atomicity.test.ts since 2026-09-09 and recorded as unproved for three days. A figure that moves because the ruler changed is not progress, and the two are separated here so nobody later reads four where the work was three. THE 2026-09-15 MOVE 136 -> 183 / 115 -> 161 IS 47 NEW LEGS FROM THREE TRACKED VERIFICATION INSTRUMENTS (ruling R-2026-09-15-03): scripts/neuter.sh, scripts/neuter_plant.mjs and scripts/predict_counts.mjs, 45 of them proved in the same change; the two registered (no-seam) are neuter.sh checks that sit behind neuter_plant.mjs refusals. gate.sh check(s) did not pass moved from registered to reached, closed by tests/compliance/runner_aggregation.test.ts, which is the injectable check list its closes_with named. A FIRST VERSION of both .mjs instruments routed refusals through a helper taking an array of messages, and this register saw no legs in neuter_plant.mjs at all: test-conventions section 2(d), reproduced while building an instrument, fixed by literal console.error at every site.

the staged-change check did not run.why: Fires only when `git diff --cached --quiet` exits above 1 -- a corrupt index or a resource failure. Planting it needs a repository whose index git cannot read, and a deliberately corrupted index is not a portable construction.
the staged-change check did not run.closes_with: A portable way to make git fail to read an index, verified on both macOS and the CI runner. Shares its seam with every other could-not-run leg in this register.

the ALTER-TABLE scan exited.closes_with: A seam that makes an input unreadable portably, verified on both macOS and the CI runner.

is unchanged after planting.why: Defence in depth behind scripts/neuter_plant.mjs, which refuses a byte-identical plant before this check can run. Reaching it needs a plant tool that reports success without writing, and the harness offers no seam to substitute one -- deliberately, since a substitutable plant tool is a hole in what the harness certifies.

no neuters selected from.why: Unreachable through the CLI: an empty name list arises only from a spec with no neuters, which scripts/neuter_plant.mjs refuses first (that refusal is reached). Kept so a future change to the name listing cannot yield a run over nothing that exits 0.

GoTrue returned a non-JSON body (HTTP.why: Fires only on a GoTrue response of a specific shape -- a non-200 from admin/generate_link, a 200 with no user id, or a non-JSON body. Reaching it needs a stub GoTrue that returns a crafted response, and no such seam exists: the script takes SUPABASE_API_URL but nothing in the repo serves a scripted reply on it. The unreachable-host leg IS planted, so the transport failure path is covered; these three are the shapes a REACHABLE but misbehaving GoTrue would produce.
GoTrue returned a non-JSON body (HTTP.closes_with: A tiny scripted HTTP responder bound to a scratch port, pointed at via SUPABASE_API_URL, returning one canned body per plant.

the ancestor check did not run (git merg.why: Fires only when `git merge-base` itself fails mid-run, after `rev-parse` and `fetch` have both succeeded. Planting it needs a seam that breaks one git invocation and not the two before it.
the ancestor check did not run (git merg.closes_with: A seam that makes a single git subcommand fail on demand -- a PATH-stubbed git that fails only for merge-base -- verified on macOS and on the CI runner.

git could not report the working tree st.why: Fires only when `git status` fails after `git rev-parse HEAD` has already succeeded in the same run. The same single-subcommand seam as above.
git could not report the working tree st.closes_with: A PATH-stubbed git that fails only for `status`, verified on both platforms.

git returned something that is not a com.why: Fires only when git exits 0 and prints something that is not a 40-hex commit. No seam produces that from a real git; it guards against a future wrapper or alias on PATH.
git returned something that is not a com.closes_with: A PATH-stubbed git that exits 0 printing a non-SHA, verified on both platforms.

a pattern match did not run (status.why: Fires only when bash cannot compile one of the scripts constant patterns, so [[ =~ ]] returns 2. Every pattern is a constant, so no plant can reach it without editing the script itself.
a pattern match did not run (status.closes_with: None planned: it exists so a pattern broken by a future edit is loud, not a silent no-match.
